questions.stem: Why do hormones only affect target cells and not all cells in the body?

options.text: Because hormones are too large to enter most cells
Because non-target cells break down the hormone immediately
Because the blood only carries hormones to specific organs
Because only target cells have specific receptors that match the hormone

questions.explanation: Although hormones travel in the blood throughout the body, they only affect cells with the correct complementary receptors on their surface. This ensures each hormone only affects its target cells.
